approach: Enforce the boundary at the lowest shared points, by remote name and by target repository. (1) athena-git gets `ORIGIN` and `require_origin`; `Git::push_branch`, `Git::push_if_remote_at` and `RecordsWriter::append_to_remote` call it first, so every records-branch push (landing sink, attribution checkpoint, cutover import) is covered. (2) athena-core remote.rs gets `require_origin`, called first in `GitRemote::push`, `replace` and `delete_branch`, plus `origin_client`, the single place landing and reconcile build their GitHub client: it reads origin's fetch and push URLs, refuses when they differ, and accepts only an https github.com URL via `GhClient::origin_repository`. `Athena::land_pr`, `try_reconcile` and early.rs use these, so a local path that merely contains `github.com` no longer yields a PR target. `GitLandingRecords::for_remote` also refuses non-origin. Tests use temp git repos with `origin` and `upstream` bare remotes and the existing `ScriptRunner`; no network. Spec entry filled and pinned by a test. CHANGELOG.md is left untouched, as criterion 7 requires.

decisions.choice: Two layers of guard: `athena_git::require_origin` in `push_branch`, `push_if_remote_at` and `append_to_remote`; `require_origin` in `GitRemote` push/replace/delete_branch (remote.rs) that calls it.
decisions.reason: Answers findings 3 and 6. All production pushes end in `Git::run(["push", ...])` in exactly these five methods (lib.rs:384-401, 432-436; remote.rs:52-79; append_to_remote reaches the first two at records_branch.rs:442-444). Its callers are landing sink (records.rs:156, 365), attribution `write_checkpoint` (attribution.rs:785) and records_import.rs:206. A guard there covers present and future callers, including `Options::with_remote` (attribution.rs:524). The guard in append_to_remote sits before `sync_from` so a refused remote is not even fetched.

rejected.why: Leaves three production push paths unguarded; the request allows any file under crates/.

rejected.why: Misses records_import.rs:206 and any future caller of append_to_remote; the shared helper is the smaller, complete cut.

decisions.reason: Every production caller passes the literal origin (landing.rs:865, early.rs:376,460, reconcile.rs:403, attribution.rs:510 DEFAULT_REMOTE). Every existing test in athena-git (lib.rs:1385-1457, records_branch.rs:846-1048), gh/tests.rs and athena-gate pushes to "origin" (searched with Grep), so no existing test breaks.

rejected.option: Compare the remote URL with the project's GitHub repository
rejected.why: A clone's origin legitimately points anywhere; the PR target is parsed from origin itself.

decisions.choice: New `origin_client(git, runner, log, ui) -> Result<GhClient>` in remote.rs, used by `Athena::land_pr` (landing.rs:865-886) and `try_reconcile` (reconcile.rs:403-412) in place of their own get-url + `parse_remote`. It uses `GhClient::origin_repository` (client.rs:1026), the strict https+host rule that early.rs already applies via `https_github_repository` (early.rs:329).
decisions.reason: Answers findings 2, 4, 8. `parse_remote` finds the host by substring (client.rs:1199), so a local mirror such as `/src/github.com/upstream-owner/project` became a PR target. One function builds the client for both landing and reconcile, so a test of it is not circular. early.rs `github_repository` also goes through the shared origin URL check. Reconcile with a lookalike path now builds no client and uses `NoHost`, so findings stay `unattributed` (reconcile.rs:284-291, 429-436).

rejected.option: Keep `parse_remote` and record the lookalike behavior as expected (previous plan)
rejected.why: It lets PRs target an upstream owner/repo from a local path and contradicts the accepted reading.
It is also tested directly (gh/tests.rs:1187-1197) and used by `origin_repository`; changing it widens the job.

decisions.choice: `origin_url` (remote.rs) reads `git remote get-url origin` and `git remote get-url --push origin` and refuses when they differ; landing, reconcile and early github_repository use it.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 5. `git push origin` honors `remote.origin.pushurl` and `pushInsteadOf`; PRs were targeted from the fetch URL. Refusing a split removes the case where the PR goes to one repository and the push to another. Direct `GitRemote` calls check the name only; the spec says so.

risks.risk: Landing and reconcile now accept only an https github.com origin (the early path already did). An SSH-style or http origin that `parse_remote` accepted (gh/tests.rs:1187-1192) is refused for landing.
risks.mitigation: Matches the system fact that SSH remotes are refused at admission and the early path's rule (early.rs:329). The error says why. Raised as a Host question. Existing land tests use the https GITHUB constant (drain.rs:3114).

risks.risk: Reconcile with a lookalike local origin loses its client, so a commit that the host could have named is reported `unattributed` (reconcile.rs:419-436).
risks.mitigation: That path never reached GitHub for a local path in a real setup. athena-cli/tests/reconcile.rs still gets `unattributed` through `NoHost`; the producer runs it.

risks.risk: The guard assumes origin is the project's own repository. A plain clone of a third-party project has origin pointing at that project, and nothing here detects it.
risks.mitigation: The spec mechanism says so, so Themis can see what is not covered. The accepted reading makes the same assumption. The guard also does not stop code that runs `git push` through `Git::run` directly outside the guarded helpers.

risks.risk: Direct `GitRemote` calls check the name only. A split push URL is refused in landing, reconcile and the early path (through `origin_url`), not inside `GitRemote::push`.
risks.mitigation: Every production `GitRemote` is built after `origin_url` has run (landing via `origin_client`, early via `github_repository`). The spec text names this limit.

(a) No origin: `origin_client` is Err, the runner has 0 calls, and no `git push` ran (a bare `upstream`/`origin` listing is unchanged). A split push URL (`git config remote.origin.pushurl <path of upstream>`) is also Err with 0 calls and upstream refs unchanged. (c) Origin `https://github.com/example/project.git`: `origin_client` returns a client for `example/project`, and calling `close_pr` (PATCH plus comment) makes calls whose path starts with `repos/example/project/` and no other repository; with an `upstream` remote present, a `GitRemote{name:"origin"}` push changes only origin's bare repository.
